text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - Leading British shares ended with moderate gains on Friday as the Dow recovered from an initial 70-point deficit as London markets closed, but dealers said the equity markets on both sides of the Atlantic remains vulnerable. The benchmark FTSE 100 share index settled 22.0 points higher at 4,236.6, as advancers led decliners 71 to 25. This was down 76.3 from last week.

FRANKFURT - German shares close bourse trade firmly ahead before release of U.S. payroll data at 1330 GMT. Dealers say buying interest returned to the market after days of declines, fuelled by enthusiasm for export shares. Volumes relatively thin and focus on U.S. for direction. The DAX index ended up 29.69 points at 3,244.93 down 184.12 from last week. In post-bourse trade the index stood at 3,235.35 up 22.53.

PARIS - French stocks ended slightly higher, snapping a three-day losing streak, after a U.S. jobs report that was roughly within market expectations. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 3.45 points or 0.14 percent to 2,517.97, down 138.71 from last Thursday.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended slightly higher in quiet trade but off best levels as markets followed U.S. Treasuries lower in the wake of latest U.S. jobs data. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) gained 2.61 points, or 0.09 percent, to close 2,836.53 a fall of 109.72 on the week.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed moderately lower on Friday, mainly depressed by continuing weakness in the brokerage and construction sectors, brokers said. A downturn on Wall Street overnight also clouded sentiment, with many dealers squaring positions ahead of key U.S. employment data due out later in the day, they said. The 225-share Nikkei average lost 268.72 points or 1.48 percent to close at 17,860.59 a drop of 349.83 from last Thursday.

HONG KONG - Solid gains in the futures market and a rally in conglomerates swept Hong Kong stocks to a higher close on Friday, but trading volume was lacklustre as the market's recent slide kept investors on edge. The Hang Seng Index closed on a gain of 149.42 points, or 1.24 percent, at 12,204.59 down 329.73 on the week.

SYDNEY - Australian shares ended a touch firmer for a second day running, led by a surging Coca-Cola Amatil in the wake of its A$3.4 billion (US$2.7 billin) Philippines soft drinks deal. The benchmark All Ordinaries index ended 8.5 points firmer at 2,369.5 a fall of 52.8 from a week ago.

JOHANNESBURG - South African stocks, already buoyant, get late shot in the arm before close from U.S. employment data and perception Wall St set to rise. Volumes healthy amid good local and foreign demand. Stocks seen flat to firming next week. Golds edge up at end, but market devoid of serious interest. The all-share index adds 34.7 points to 7,015.8 a drop of 7.9 from a week ago as the industrials index puts on 36.8 points to 8,239.1 down 100.3 since last week. The golds index edges up 2.3 points to 1,291.3. This was down 10.3 from last Thursday.
